title: The tab bar overflows instead of scrolling: tabs and the + button run off the pane
problem: Each tab is `.flex_1().min_w(ui(80.)).max_w(ui(240.))` (src/finder/tab_bar.rs:319-323) and the bar is a plain `h_flex().h(36).flex_shrink_0().px(10).gap(6)` with the + button after the tabs (tab_bar.rs:405-426). Nothing scrolls, clips or shrinks further, so once N tabs need more than the pane (about 86N + 42pt) the last tabs and the + button are laid out past the pane's right edge. That is the 10th tab in the default 1100pt window (888pt beside the 212pt sidebar), the 7th at the 850pt minimum window (src/lib.rs:422), and the 4th tab in split view's main pane at the default size (337.5pt, src/workspace.rs:299-316), where the overflow lands under the second pane. Tabs past the edge cannot be clicked or closed with the mouse, and + is unreachable. The toolbar and scope bar both handle running out of room (src/finder/toolbar.rs:98-116; src/finder/bars.rs:62-63); the tab bar does not.
proposal: In `render_tab_bar` put the tabs in their own strip, `h_flex().id("tabs").flex_1().min_w_0().gap(ui(6.)).overflow_x_scroll().track_scroll(&scroll)`, and keep `new-tab` outside it with `.flex_shrink_0()` so it is always reachable. Keep the `ScrollHandle` on the Workspace (new field with a getter), because each tab's own Finder draws the bar (workspace.rs:284-288) and the position should survive switching tabs. Scroll the active tab into view (`ScrollHandle::scroll_to_item(active)`) from `new_tab`, `select_tab`, `close_tab` and `move_tab` (workspace.rs:171-229). Optionally let tabs narrow to about 56pt before the strip scrolls. The sidebar's sideways scroller (src/finder/sidebar.rs:403-411) is the pattern to copy.
original_test_plan: Headless UI test with `with_tabs` (tests/basics.rs:21): `ui.resize(850., 600.)`, press Cmd+T nine times, then assert `ui.snapshot("new-tab").bounds().right() <= ui.snapshot("tab-bar").bounds().right()` and that the active tab's bounds lie inside the `tabs` strip. Both fail today, since ten 80pt tabs cannot fit 638pt. Press `ctrl-tab` to wrap to the first tab and assert it is scrolled inside the strip. `examples/screenshot.rs --tabs N` gives a picture to check by eye.
original_risks: A scrolling strip has no visible affordance beyond the cut-off tab; a fade or chevron could follow later. Dragging a tab onto one that is scrolled out of view will not auto-scroll. Edits `render_tab_bar`, as the tab-drop-and-close candidate does, so do them together.

verifier.claim_check:
The claim holds as written; I could not refute it.

- **Tab sizing:** each tab is `.flex_1().min_w(ui(80.)).max_w(ui(240.))` (src/finder/tab_bar.rs:319-323), so it cannot shrink below 80pt.
- **Bar:** `h_flex().id("tab-bar").h(36).flex_shrink_0().px(10).gap(6)` with the tabs then `new-tab` as children (tab_bar.rs:405-426). It has no overflow style, no wrap and no scroll handle.
- **Ancestors don't clip:** the bar sits in `v_flex().flex_1().h_full().min_w_0()` (src/finder/mod.rs:3177-3182), under the `finder` root (mod.rs:3042-3047) and the workspace's pane div (src/workspace.rs:300-304). None of them clips.
- **No other handler:** nothing in `src` caps the tab count or scrolls the bar. A grep for `overflow_x_scroll|track_scroll|ScrollHandle` finds nothing in tab_bar.rs or workspace.rs.

The arithmetic checks out: the bar needs 20 (padding) + 80N + 6N (gaps) + 22 (the + button) = 86N + 42.

| Situation | Room for the bar | First tab that overflows |
|---|---|---|
| Default 1100pt window (src/lib.rs:371), 212pt sidebar (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:164) | 888pt | 10th |
| 850pt minimum window (src/lib.rs:422) | 638pt | 7th |
| Split view at default size | 337.5pt | 4th |
| Split view at 850pt | 212.5pt | 2 tabs already need 214pt |

Split view is this tight because `sidebar_width_shown` clamps against the window width, not the pane (src/finder/sidebar.rs:193-200). A larger Text size setting makes every case worse, since `ui()` scales.

In split view the second pane is drawn after the main pane (workspace.rs:306-315) with an opaque background (mod.rs:3047), so it covers the overflowing tabs and takes their clicks.

Not intentional and not already covered:
- docs/manual.md:156 describes click, ×, drag and + with no limit; line 160 documents only the toolbar folding.
- CHANGELOG.md has no entry about it.
- The sibling bars do cope: `ToolbarFit::for_room` (src/finder/toolbar.rs:98-116) and `.flex_wrap()` on the scope bar (src/finder/bars.rs:62-63).
- No test pins the overflow. tests/file_ops.rs:1031-1092 only uses two tabs; `new-tab` is never used as a selector.
verifier.implementation_notes:
The proposal is sound; these are refinements. Nothing here was compiled or run (read-only review).

**1. src/workspace.rs**
- Add a field `tab_scroll: ScrollHandle`, set to `ScrollHandle::new()` in the only constructor (workspace.rs:75), with a getter `pub fn tab_scroll(&self) -> &ScrollHandle`.
- Put one call, `self.tab_scroll.scroll_to_item(self.active)`, in `tabs_changed` (workspace.rs:284). `new_tab`, `select_tab` (and so `step_tab`), `close_tab` (and so `move_tab_to_new_window`) and `move_tab` all end there, so four call sites are unnecessary.
- Keeping the handle on the Workspace is right: each tab's Finder draws the bar under its own element state, but `track_scroll` shares the handle's offset.

**2. src/finder/tab_bar.rs `render_tab_bar`**
- Clone the handle inside the existing `host.read(cx)` block (lines 282-302).
- Wrap the tabs in a strip:
  `h_flex().id("tabs").flex_1().min_w_0().max_w(ui(n as f32 * 240. + (n - 1) as f32 * 6.)).gap(ui(6.)).overflow_x_scroll().track_scroll(&scroll).children(tabs).test_support()`
- Keep `new-tab` as the bar's last child and add `.flex_shrink_0()`.
- Tabs keep `.flex_1().min_w(80).max_w(240)`. The strip's children are exactly the tabs, so child index equals tab index for `scroll_to_item`.

**3. Correction: add the `max_w`.** The proposal's bare `flex_1()` strip would push + to the pane's right edge whenever there are few tabs. Today it sits right after the last tab, because tabs cap at 240pt. The `max_w` keeps today's look until the tabs fill the bar.

**4. Do not copy `.restrict_scroll_to_axis()` from the sidebar scroller** (src/finder/sidebar.rs:407). Without it, gpui maps a plain vertical wheel to x on an x-only scroller (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/div.rs:3413-3421). With it, mouse-wheel users could not scroll the tabs at all. The proposal's snippet omits it correctly, but "the pattern to copy" would bring it in.

**5. Pitfall: `scroll_to_item` is silently dropped on the bar's first frame.**
- `scroll_to_active_item` runs in prepaint (div.rs:2065-2067) before `clamp_scroll_position` records this frame's `overflow` and `bounds` on the handle (div.rs:2505, 2542).
- On the first frame the strip is drawn, `overflow.x` is still `Visible`, so the request is consumed without scrolling (div.rs:4432-4447).
- This is harmless going from 1 to 2 tabs. It matters only when several tabs open in one frame from a one-tab window (`open_in_new_tabs` with several folders, src/finder/menus.rs:108) in a narrow pane.
- Either accept that, or re-request on the next frame when `tab_scroll.bounds()` is still empty.
- For the same reason, do not add a `scroll_to_item` to `toggle_split`: it would use the pre-split strip width.

**6. Skip the optional 56pt minimum.** After 20pt of padding, the gap and the × button, about 15pt of title is left.

**7. Things that already work and need no code**
- gpui clamps the offset each frame when tabs close or the window widens (div.rs:2526-2537).
- The mask for an x-only scroller leaves y unclipped (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/style.rs:638), so the active tab's border is not cut.
- Context menus and drag inside a scroller already work for sidebar rows.

**8. Docs**
- Add one sentence to docs/manual.md:156: when the tabs don't fit, the tab bar scrolls sideways, the tab you switch to scrolls into view, and + stays in reach.
- Extend the tests/basics.rs line at manual.md:1288.
- Add a CHANGELOG.md `[Unreleased]` › Fixed entry.

If the tab-drop-and-close candidate also edits `render_tab_bar`, land them together.
verifier.test_plan:
Add a headless UI test to tests/basics.rs, in the "new tabs" section (line 250), for example `#[gpui_kit::test] fn many_tabs_scroll_and_plus_stays_in_reach`.

**Harness helpers**
- `Fixture::new` and `with_tabs` (basics.rs:21).
- From tests/common/mod.rs: `Ui::resize` (545), `Ui::press` with `cmd("t")`, `Ui::snapshot(id).bounds()` and `.visible()` (626), `Ui::click`, `Ui::scroll` (465).
- `visible()` is the element's bounds clipped by the content mask and the viewport (gpui-base-0.8.1/src/test_support.rs:471-479), so it reads false for a tab scrolled out of the strip or past the window.
- `click` itself panics on an element that is not visible (gpui-kit-0.8.1/src/test.rs:153).
- The strip needs `.test_support()` so `"tabs"` can be found.

**Steps**
1. `ui.resize(850., 600.)`, then press `cmd("t")` nine times: 10 tabs, the last one active. The strip is 590pt and the tabs need 854pt.
2. Assert `ui.snapshot("new-tab").visible()` and that its `bounds().right()` is at most `ui.snapshot("tab-bar").bounds().right()`. This fails today: the + sits at about x=1104 in an 850pt window.
3. Assert `("tab", 9usize)` is visible and its bounds lie inside `ui.snapshot("tabs").bounds()`. Assert `("tab", 0usize)` is not visible.
4. `ui.press("ctrl-tab")` wraps to tab 0. Assert tab 0's left edge is at or right of the strip's left edge and that it is visible.
5. `ui.scroll("tabs", point(px(0.), px(-200.)))`, a plain vertical wheel. Assert tab 0's `origin.x` decreased; this guards against `restrict_scroll_to_axis`.
6. `ui.click("new-tab")` and assert the workspace has 11 tabs with the new one visible. Then `ui.click(("close-tab", 10usize))` and assert 10 tabs.
7. Split-view case: at the default size, press `cmd("\\")` with 4 tabs and assert `new-tab` is visible and inside `tab-bar`. `split-pane` has no `test_support()`, so compare against `tab-bar`.
8. Guard for the + position: with 2 tabs at a wide size (`ui.resize(1100., 700.)`), assert `new-tab`'s left edge is within about 7pt of `("tab", 1usize)`'s right edge.

**Existing tests that must stay green**
- tests/file_ops.rs:1031 `tabs_and_split_view`: drags `("tab",1)` onto `("tab",0)` and clicks `("tab",1)`. Ids are looked up by leaf id, so the extra `"tabs"` level should not matter.
- tests/basics.rs:253 `folders_open_in_new_tabs`.
- The `with_tabs` tests in tests/settings.rs.

`examples/screenshot.rs --tabs N [--split]` renders with Metal, so it is a by-eye check on macOS only.
verifier.risks:
- **No visible cue:** nothing shows that more tabs exist beyond the cut-off tab at the strip's edge. A fade or chevron could follow later.
- **Accidental scrolling:** a vertical wheel or trackpad swipe over the tab bar now scrolls the tabs. This is the usual convention, but it is new behaviour.
- **No auto-scroll while dragging:** a tab cannot be dragged onto one that is scrolled out of view.
- **First-frame edge case:** if several tabs are opened at once from a one-tab window in a narrow pane, the active tab can start out of view until the next tab switch (see pitfall 5 in the notes).
- **Split or resize does not re-reveal the active tab:** turning on split view or narrowing the window can leave it scrolled out; the user has to scroll.
- **Layout is unverified:** the strip's `max_w` and the flex behaviour were reasoned from the gpui and taffy sources, not run. The geometry assertions in the test are the check.
- **Merge conflict:** this overlaps any other candidate that edits `render_tab_bar`.
